findings.reason: the section must state whether abort reuses the existing retryable family or adds one (and, if it adds, name what it retires/merges), because that choice also fixes the retry behaviour the section relies on.
findings.text: §22 raises "a retryable error carrying the finish reason" for `finish_reason="abort"` "beside the existing EmptyResponseError handling of length", which is a new error/refusal family (an aborted reply is non-empty, so it cannot be the existing `EmptyResponseError`, whose contract is "no usable content"); the section neither names a family it retires or merges nor states why nothing can be, against a brief reporting refusal_families 0 — and the ambiguity is load-bearing because retryability is decided by substring match on the message in `_is_retryable` (`RETRYABLE_PATTERNS`, llm.py:693), so whether the abort error is a new class or an extension of the existing family determines whether the retry loop actually retries it

findings.reason: the plan should derive the mapping from the call sites (or a registry the call sites read) so the pin cannot disagree with the binding it guards, rather than restating it.
findings.text: §22 proposes "a test [that] maps each discovery call site's prompt to its response model", which would store the prompt↔response-model binding a third time: it already lives authoritatively at every call site (`call_llm_structured(prompt_name, response_model=...)`, e.g. `paths/scorer.py:137,143`, `code/workers.py:298`, `wiki/scoring.py:505`) and, for the schema defaults, in `_DEFAULT_SCHEMA_NEEDS`/`_SCHEMA_PROVIDERS` (`imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py:893,1056`); a hand-maintained test table can drift from those call sites, which is the exact defect the pin exists to prevent

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — neither design adds a module; §22 lands its behaviour in the existing structured-call loops of `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py` and §14 in the existing owners `imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py` and `imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py`, so the surface stays the same while the behaviour moves into existing deep owners.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §22's prompt-to-response-model pin restates a binding already owned by each call site invocation.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §22 adds an LLM error family without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §22 extends the existing `schema_needs` frontmatter and shared-partial mechanism (`imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py:1361`, `_SCHEMA_PROVIDERS` registry at `:893`) and the existing `EmptyResponseError(finish_reason)` / `finish_reason == "length"` retry handling in `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:475,2318`, and §14 extends `reset_to_status` and the single `render_path_prefix_clause` renderer instead of adding parallel machinery — every mechanism the plan names was opened and found.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §14's `path_prefixes` parameter on `reset_to_status` is a consolidation (it removes the hand-wired inline block at `imas_codex/cli/discover/paths.py:249-253`) rather than a new parallel layer, and §22's abort branch is a classification inside the retry loop, not a wrapper over it.
